javascript.details: Animation registration stores at most one persistent callback and returns handle 1; missing context, callback, timer allocation, or invalid timer arguments return undefined. Callback exceptions are printed and reported to the host frame loop without throwing through C.

lua.details: Animation methods require a Lua function and raise on invalid input. Only one persistent registry callback is stored; callback errors are printed and make the host call return false. Lua exposes no timer table.

wasmtime.details: There are no animation or timer host imports. An optional guest-exported frame(f32) function is called every host frame; traps/errors are recorded and printed, and the host call returns false.

browser_wasm.details: There are no animation or timer host imports. The browser runner calls an optional guest-exported frame function every requestAnimationFrame tick; a guest exception is not converted to a sentinel by the frame closure.

state_ownership.javascript: JSCanvasContext owns one duplicated animation callback and a growable timer array of duplicated callbacks. Context destruction releases every live callback; the host processes animation, timers, and pending Promise jobs once per frame.
state_ownership.lua: LuaCanvasContext owns one animation callback registry reference and releases it on replacement, cancellation, or context destruction.
state_ownership.wasmtime: WasmCanvasContext borrows the instantiated guest frame function and invokes it through the owning store/context; the guest module owns its exported function.
state_ownership.browser_wasm: BudoWasmRunner owns the instantiated module reference and calls its optional frame export from the browser requestAnimationFrame loop.

details: Managed JavaScript timers are driven by the Budo frame timestamp, not browser setTimeout/setInterval.
Lua exposes animation.start in addition to requestFrame/cancelFrame but has no timer namespace.
Browser-native WebAssembly receives no scheduling imports and instead optionally exports frame; the same direction applies to Wasmtime.
Managed requestFrame callbacks are persistent until replaced or canceled, unlike the browser DOM requestAnimationFrame one-shot contract.
The host calls managed animation callbacks and JavaScript timers explicitly; Wasmtime frame is discovered from the guest module and receives an f32 millisecond timestamp.

operations.name: animation_start
operations.signature: (callback(timestamp_ms)) -> void; replace the persistent Lua frame callback

operations.name: request_frame
operations.signature: (callback(timestamp_ms)) -> handle 1; replace the persistent managed frame callback

operations.name: cancel_frame
operations.signature: (handle ignored) -> void; clear the single managed frame callback

operations.name: timer_once
operations.signature: (delay_ms:number, callback) -> timer id or undefined; non-positive delay fires on a later timer-processing pass

operations.name: timer_every
operations.signature: (interval_ms:number, callback) -> timer id or undefined; interval is clamped to at least 1 ms

operations.name: timer_clear
operations.signature: (timer_id:i32) -> void; unknown or inactive ids are ignored

operations.name: guest_frame
operations.signature: optional guest export frame(timestamp_ms); invoked once per host frame
